To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
amphiphilic copolymer derivatives are effective against the microorganism and do not cause haemolytic activity for mammalian erytrocytes.
a series of amphiphilic copolymers with different molar ratios of the monomers were synthesized and the copolymer 30:70 exhibited the best antimicrobial activity against the microorganisms.
amphiphilic copolymer with molar ratio of glycidyl methacylate and styrene monomers 30/70 was found to be the most effective against microorganisms.

the synthesis and antimicrobial activity of amphiphilic copolymer derivatives.
the synthesis of amphiphilic copolymer derivatives and their antimicrobial activities.
the synthesis of a series of amphiphilic copolymers with different molar ratios of monomers.

the copolymers have good potential for application as antibacterial materials in medical and industrial fields.
amphiphilic copolymer derivatives are effective antimicrobial agents against gram-negative, gram-positive bacteria, and fungus.
the copolymeric derivatives have good antimicrobial activity, and the antimicrobial activity was related to the molar ratio, the structure of the copolymer and its molecular weight.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antimicrobial activity of amphiphilic copolymers is dependent on the molecular structure of copolymers.

the antimicrobial activity of amphiphilic copolymers is dependent on the hydrophobicity of their side chains, and the amphiphilic polymers with a higher hydrophilic/lipophilic balance are more effective.
the amphiphilic copolymers with quaternized groups are promising antimicrobial agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the copolymeric quaternized derivatives of glycidyl methacylate and styrene have antimicrobial activity against the tested microorganism and do not have any haemo-toxicity.
amphiphilic polymers are effective against gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria and fungi, and they have no haemolytic activity.
the copolymers have potential for use as antimicrobial agents in the medical field and the pharmaceutical industry.
